model.definition: native/frame_clock.h: FrameClock::frame(now_ms, refresh_rate, pacing, consumer) returns whether this Godot frame is a tick
model.rule: tick = consumer && (pacing == Presentation || due); due = !served || now - previous_frame >= T / 2 || now - last_tick >= T; T = 1000 / R ms
model.rate: R is the refresh rate the display reports for the window's screen when it is positive and finite (rateSource display), 60 otherwise (rateSource fallback)
model.presentation: a window with V-Sync enabled or adaptive on a real display: every frame with a consumer is a tick
model.time: headless, V-Sync disabled or mailbox, or unknown: the due rule above
model.consumer: pending frame callbacks, or a Native Animated backend that asked for frames and has not asked to pause (NativeAnimated::active)
ticked: requestAnimationFrame callbacks, with the tick's timestamp
RN's Native Animated backend frame, with the same timestamp
model.snapshot: frameClock {periodMs, refreshRate, rateSource, pacing, pacingSource, frames, ticks, skippedFrames, lastFrameMs, lastTickMs}
properties: two ticks are never closer than T / 2 under Time pacing
a loop capped at the refresh or slower ticks on every frame while its jitter stays under T / 2
a loop faster than T / 2 ticks about once per T
a stall gives one late tick and the catch-up frames behind it wait
after idling the first frame with a consumer ticks at once

headedObservationsOutsideTheReceipt.description: A scratch script (not retained) ran the application with the frame-clock probe's requestAnimationFrame loop in a real macOS window and read the application's snapshot once per Godot frame. The suite asserts none of it.
headedObservationsOutsideTheReceipt.machine: MacBook Pro M3 Pro, a 120 Hz ProMotion display, Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility renderer
headedObservationsOutsideTheReceipt.rendererReadback: window_set_vsync_mode with ADAPTIVE or MAILBOX reads back ENABLED on this renderer; DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate reported 120.0 and costs about 0.35 microseconds a call

regressions.note: Every native-cold-start suite step after Godot install and npm run setup, in the workflow's order, plus test:examples and test:recovery, from the committed tree; every step passed on its first run

sdkAndAdapters.outputDirectories: fresh build/*-stageb directories for codegen-native-compile, native-sdk, adapter-registry, adapter-loader and adapter-runtime (deleted after the run); test:consumer, test:cold and parity:godot used their own

limits: Timers (setTimeout, setInterval) still run on every Godot frame: they are not quantized to ticks, as RN's iOS and Android timers are quantized to display frames. The baseline check 'A zero-delay interval fires once on every Godot frame, tick or not' records it.

A Presentation tick carries the CPU time of its Godot frame, so the steps between ticks are as uneven as those frames and a decay lands lower than at a regular cadence (the presentation-bimodal lane ends about 1 px short of the Time lanes); the iOS display link hands RN the regular targetTimestamp, which is not implemented.
ADAPTIVE and MAILBOX V-Sync are mapped by detect_pacing and covered by the unit test only: the Compatibility renderer of this Mac reads both back as ENABLED.

Real displays are not certified: the lanes are headless and state V-Sync presentation and the refresh rate through validation seams; the headed observations are one exploratory run each on one 120 Hz Mac, outside the receipt.
Variable refresh rates, external screens, OS suspend and resume, behavior under JS load, frame budgets (GF-30) and Godot Android and iOS exports are not covered.
The clock has no visual output: there is no example scene and no capture.
No whole GF, checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closed: GF-05 and GF-19 are not at their first slice, so their slice checkpoints, already closed, do not change.

stutterObservationsOutsideTheReceipt.description: A scratch harness (not retained) froze and thawed (SIGSTOP and SIGCONT) the Godot process that ran the probe, with random durations, so that its frames came as on a hosted runner: a stall, then frames close behind it. It ran each suite on the committed tree with the retained controls present. The suite asserts none of it.
